clue.text: Child inclined to sound hesitant at this stage in life

parts.note: CH is the standard abbreviation for child
apt means inclined or likely to do something
er is the noise of someone hesitating

explanation.surface: A child at a certain age who has started stammering and hesitating when speaking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Child' looks like the definition, but it supplies only the opening abbreviation; the definition sits at the far end.
explanation.definitionFit: A period of someone's life can be called a chapter, borrowing the term for a section of a book.

clue.text: Preference for cold house leads to chill

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap
HO is the abbreviation for house
to ice something is to chill it

explanation.surface: Someone who prefers a cold house ends up feeling chilly.
explanation.definitionFit: Your choice is what you select, the option you prefer, so it is a preference.

clue.text: Ill-disposed towards a piece of poetry

parts.note: taken as written
a verse is a piece of poetry

explanation.surface: Someone who dislikes a particular poem.
explanation.definitionFit: Being averse to something means opposing or disliking it, being ill-disposed to it.

clue.text: Equal number beat time beforehand

indicators.note: beforehand says the later pieces of the clue go ahead of the first one

parts.note: to tan someone's hide is to beat them
T is the abbreviation for time
an amount is a number or quantity

explanation.surface: Reads like instructions for a musician to keep the beat in advance.
explanation.definitionFit: Tantamount to means equivalent in effect, the same as equal to.

clue.text: Brisk run then a swim back

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run
taken as written

indicators.note: back means going the other way, so the swim word is read right to left

parts.note: a dip is a quick swim

explanation.surface: A quick jog followed by a swim to finish, like a triathlete's routine.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapid means fast, and brisk means quick and energetic.

clue.text: Plucky girl left before worker

indicators.note: before tells us the earlier pieces sit ahead of the final piece in the answer

parts.note: gal is an informal word for a girl
L is the abbreviation for left
the worker ant is the crossword's favourite worker

explanation.surface: A brave young woman who quit her job ahead of a colleague.
explanation.definitionFit: Gallant describes someone brave and spirited, the same courage as being plucky.

clue.text: Arena actor pleased at Rio cavorting

parts.note: glad means pleased

indicators.note: cavorting means leaping about wildly, so those letters jump into another order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A happy performer dancing in a stadium in Rio de Janeiro.
explanation.definitionFit: A gladiator fought in the Roman amphitheatre, performing for the crowd in the arena.

clue.text: Was untruthful about deli?

indicators.note: about suggests things moved around, so the word's letters are turned into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Asks whether someone fibbed about the delicatessen.
explanation.definitionFit: To have lied is to have said something false, the past tense of being untruthful.

clue.text: Drivers accept police corruption resulting in personal loss

indicators.note: to accept is to take in, so the drivers' letters hold the others

parts.note: the AA, Automobile Association, is a British motoring organisation for drivers

indicators.note: corruption is a debasing or twisting, so the letters are twisted into another order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Motorists paying police bribes and losing out personally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Personal loss' sounds like bereavement; the loss is of hair.
explanation.definitionFit: Alopecia is a medical condition of hair loss, a very personal kind of loss.

clue.text: Express disapproval as the final student takes time to get guidance

parts.note: tut is the clicking noise of disapproval

indicators.note: final points to the last letter only of the word it qualifies

parts.note: its last letter
L for learner, as on a learner driver's plate
an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: A tutor frowning while the last pupil takes ages to be helped.
explanation.definitionFit: Tutelage is instruction or protection given by a tutor or guardian, so guidance.

clue.text: Canoe breaks up in sea

indicators.note: something that breaks up falls to pieces, so its letters can be put back together in another order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A small boat being smashed apart out on the open water.
explanation.definitionFit: An ocean is a vast body of salt water, a near synonym for the sea.

clue.text: Did away with stepdaughter abroad

parts.note: split as step and daughter: a step in a process is a phase, and D is the abbreviation for daughter
abroad can mean out and about, outside

explanation.surface: Reads like a dark tale of getting rid of a stepdaughter by sending her overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface welds 'step' and 'daughter' into one relative; split them and each supplies its own piece.
explanation.definitionFit: To phase something out is to discontinue it gradually, which means doing away with it.

clue.text: Clownish property of foreign aid, pre-cuts

indicators.note: foreign suggests something strange and unfamiliar, so the letters take an unfamiliar new order

parts.note: taken as written, punctuation ignored

explanation.surface: Political jargon about overseas aid budgets before spending cuts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Property' is meant in the theatrical sense, a prop.
explanation.definitionFit: A custard pie thrown in the face is a classic slapstick prop used by circus clowns.

clue.text: Managed to return without a lot

indicators.note: to return is to go back, so the word is read from its end to its start
without in its old sense means outside, so one piece wraps round the other

parts.note: led means managed or directed
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone coped with going back without much to show for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' looks like 'lacking', but here it means outside. 'Lot' is in the sense of 'a great deal'.
explanation.definitionFit: A deal, as in 'a good deal', is a large quantity, just as a lot is.

clue.text: Divided objects cause wavering

parts.note: something divided is cut in two
to mind is to object, as in 'do you mind?'

explanation.surface: Splitting objects up leads to indecision.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in two minds is an idiom for being undecided, wavering between options.

clue.text: Unpaid support provided during excursion

indicators.note: during places one thing inside the span of another, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: an outing is a trip or excursion
a stand is a support, as for a music score

explanation.surface: A trip on which helpers were given but nobody got paid.
explanation.definitionFit: A debt that is outstanding has not yet been settled, so it remains unpaid.

clue.text: Restaurant with alternative atmosphere and ostentatious paintings

indicators.note: alternative suggests taking the other way, so everything after it is read from the end backwards

parts.note: air is atmosphere or ambience
OTT, over the top, means ostentatious
paintings are art

explanation.surface: A review of an eatery with a bohemian vibe and showy pictures on the walls.
explanation.definitionFit: A trattoria is a simple Italian eating place, a kind of restaurant.

clue.text: A little and often becomes unacceptable

parts.note: a bit means a little
much can mean often, as in 'do you go there much?'

explanation.surface: A small thing done too frequently grows intolerable.
explanation.definitionFit: Calling something a bit much is an idiom saying it is excessive and not acceptable.

clue.text: Following directions I am to carry trunks

indicators.note: following means coming after, so the compass pieces come first and the rest after them

parts.note: S and W, south and west, are compass directions
I'm is short for I am
to carry clothes is to wear them, as in carrying a look

explanation.surface: Someone obeying instructions to lug heavy luggage chests.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trunks' looks like luggage to be carried, but it means swimming shorts.
explanation.definitionFit: Swimming trunks are an example of clothing worn for bathing.

clue.text: Weapon fired erratically down a mound of earth outside

indicators.note: outside says the earthwork goes round the shuffled letters

parts.note: a barrow is an ancient burial mound

indicators.note: something fired erratically goes all over the place, so the letters scatter into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An archer's wild shot falling short onto a grassy hump.
explanation.definitionFit: The bow and arrow is a classic ranged weapon of archers and hunters.

clue.text: Egghead to announce development

parts.note: read as egg's head, the first letter of egg
to state is to declare or announce

explanation.surface: A brainy person preparing to declare a breakthrough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Egghead' reads as an intellectual but splits into egg's head.
explanation.definitionFit: A housing estate is a development of homes built together on one site.

clue.text: Agreement with international organisation is working

parts.note: the UN is the United Nations
taken as written
on means working, as a switched-on machine

explanation.surface: A global body is busy forging a treaty.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting in unison means acting together in harmony, in agreement.

clue.text: Finds some pasta meals to be dull

indicators.note: finding some of a phrase means taking just a portion sitting inside the words

parts.note: running across the two words

explanation.surface: A diner's verdict that plates of pasta are bland and boring.
explanation.definitionFit: Tame means unexciting or insipid, a synonym for dull.

clue.text: Rock artist?

parts.note: surface reading: a musician who plays rock music
setter's reading: a craftsman whose material is literal rock, who cuts and dresses building blocks

explanation.definitionFit: A tradesman who shapes stone is a skilled artisan whose medium is rock.

clue.text: Reminder: no escapes from dreadful dungeon!

indicators.note: dreadful means in a terrible state, so the remaining letters are jumbled
escapes means gets out, so the named letters leave the word

parts.note: taken as written: the letters to remove
taken as written

explanation.surface: A warning that nobody gets out of this awful prison.
explanation.walkthrough: One N and the O go from the prison word, leaving five letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A nudge is a gentle prompt, something that reminds someone to act.

clue.text: See the point

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to notice or catch sight of
second meaning: a particular place or location

explanation.surface: Understand what is being argued.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means to catch sight of as a verb, and as a noun a precise place, like 'the spot'.

clue.text: Former piano found in ruined building was still working

indicators.note: found in tells us the first pieces sit inside the other letters
building means constructing, so the word before it is put together anew in another order

parts.note: taken as written
ex means former
P is the musical notation for piano, softly

explanation.surface: An old piano discovered in a derelict building still played.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ruined building' reads as a wreck, but 'ruined' is the raw material and 'building' the signal to rebuild it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unexpired has not reached its end date, so it is still valid and in force.

clue.text: Approaches seedy areas to north

indicators.note: placed to the north means at the top, which in an across answer means first

parts.note: N is the abbreviation for north
ears are the seed-bearing heads of cereal plants such as corn

explanation.surface: Someone drawing close to a run-down part of town in the north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seedy' suggests squalid, but here it is literal: ears of wheat are the parts full of seeds.
explanation.definitionFit: To near a place is to come closer to it, so nears means approaches.

clue.text: Breathe out and have a drink

indicators.note: out can mean wrong or not in place, so the letters are set in a different order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A calming routine: exhale slowly, then relax with a cuppa.
explanation.definitionFit: An infusion of herbs in hot water, such as camomile, is a drink.

clue.text: Each part of ship is of oriental origin

parts.note: EA is the abbreviation for each
the stern is the rear part of a ship

explanation.surface: Every section of a vessel turns out to have come from Asia.
explanation.definitionFit: Oriental refers to the East, so something of oriental origin is eastern.
